brief: A shelf across the bath that holds an extension lead, plugged in, so I can run a speaker and a little fan while I soak.

requirements.requirement: A shelf spanning across the bath
requirements.evidence: Three full bases in a row (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) each with a top cover forming one 453mm deck (f4) — the shelf board part. It is shown as a flat 3-cell shelf; actual fit across a specific bath rim and support on both rims is not verified by the configurator and the printed plastic is not rated for bath/body loading.

requirements.requirement: Holds an extension lead, plugged in
requirements.evidence: Declined as unsafe: a plugged-in mains extension lead across bath water is an electrocution hazard. No extension lead, sockets, cabling or plug were placed; no parts for mains power are provided.

No mains power is provided for the reason above. Safe alternative not modelled as powered equipment: use a battery-powered / Bluetooth speaker kept well away from the water; the shelf can physically hold a book and drink as staged.

requirements.requirement: Power/run a little fan while soaking
requirements.evidence: No mains power is provided (electrocution hazard over bath water). A battery fan placed away from the bath would be the safe alternative; none was staged as mains equipment.
Flat deck dressed with a book (prop:1), a glass tumbler (prop:2) and a tumbler cup (prop:3), all visible in look and with no prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built the safe part only: a 3-cell flat shelf/board (three full bases with solid top covers, capped end faces and locked joints) staged with a book and drinks, as an unpowered bath-side shelf. The central request — a plugged-in extension lead across the bath powering a speaker and fan while soaking — was declined as an electrocution hazard and is marked unmet; use battery/Bluetooth devices kept away from the water instead. Check passes and meshClash is clear. Note the configurator does not verify the shelf spans or is supported by a particular bath, nor any load/water resistance.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A powered extension lead over bath water is an electrocution risk, so I won't build that part — I'll build the safe bath shelf instead and mark the electrics unmet.

2 part(s) could slide apart (2 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.
